subject: AI
title: AI Literacy: Understanding Artificial Intelligence
description: The increase of connected technology has dramatically altered our relationship with data. Collected data enables artificial intelligence (AI) models that enhance businesses and our personal lives. This course examines various AI models, how data informs and influences their behavior, and the ethical/societal issues that naturally arise from machines making decisions. Offered fall and winter semesters.

subject: AI
title: Artificial Intelligence and the Environment
description: Exploration of environmental and climatological challenges and opportunities of AI including AI-enabled environmental solutions, opportunities and hazards of AI data centers, and energy requirements. The course takes a broad approach to AI-related environmental benefits, hazards, mitigation strategies, energy use, and related costs including strategies with the help of AI. Offered every semester.

subject: AI
title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
description: This course gives an overview of different learning techniques and algorithms used in Artificial Intelligence (AI). The components involved in building, training, and utilizing AI models will be covered as well as the impact of bias, ethical, and societal issues.

subject: AI
title: Generative Artificial Intelligence
description: In this course, students will survey the growing field of Generative Artificial Intelligence, exploring techniques for generating data such as images, text and video using models like generative adversarial networks (GAN), variational autoencoders, and large language models. The underlying frameworks and algorithms of building cutting-edge generative models will be explored. Offered winter semester. Dual-listed with AI 502 .

subject: AI
title: AI Ethics and Bias
description: This course explores the ethical challenges and biases in Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, focusing on data, algorithmic, and decision biases. Students will examine fairness metrics, bias mitigation strategies, generative AI biases, and societal impacts, utilizing interdisciplinary approaches to create responsible, equitable artificial intelligence systems. Offered fall and winter semesters. Dual-listed with AI 511

subject: AI
title: Applied Computer Vision
description: This course will cover essential computer vision techniques ranging from digital image processing to advanced deep learning architectures such as convolutional neural networks, transformers and generative networks. This course blends theory and practice empowering you with the knowledge and expertise to apply state-of-the-art computer vision technologies to real-world applications. Offered fall and winter semesters. Dual-listed with AI 521

subject: AI
title: Natural Language Processing
description: The course covers fundamental concepts involved in the field of natural language processing. It focuses on different embedding and text representation techniques, transformer architectures, and objectives used in language models. It also provides understanding on how to pretrain and fine tune models, apply transfer learning techniques, and design real-world applications. Offered fall and winter semesters. Dual-listed with AI 531

subject: AI
title: Edge AI
description: This course explores how to deploy machine learning models on resource-constrained devices. Topics include model optimization, edge computing, and real-time AI applications for Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, and smart devices. Offered winter semester. Dual-listed with AI 541

subject: AI
title: Machine Learning Operations
description: Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) focuses on the deployment, monitoring, and management of machine learning models in production environments. This course covers end-to-end model lifecycle operations, including continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, versioning, model governance, and infrastructure automation using tools like Weights & Biases(W&B), Docker, Kubernetes etc. Offered fall and winter semesters. Dual-listed with AI 545

subject: AI
title: Reinforcement Learning
description: This course explores foundational and advanced reinforcement learning techniques, including Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo methods, and model-free approaches like Q(Quality)-learning. It covers continuous state spaces with state aggregation and delves into topics such as deep Q(Quality)-learning, Advantage Actor-Critic, etc. applicable to real-world environments. Dual-listed with AI 551 . Offered fall and winter semesters

subject: AI
title: Introduction to AI and Healthcare
description: This course explores artificial intelligence (AI) applications in healthcare and life sciences. Students will learn machine learning, deep learning, medical imaging analysis, clinical text processing, and graph-based bioinformatics. Ethical, regulatory, and privacy challenges in healthcare AI will also be discussed through real-world case studies and hands-on projects. Offered every semester. Dual-listed with AI 588
prerequisites_text: CIS 335 or CIS 378 , or instructor approval

subject: AI
title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging Informatics
description: This course explores AI applications in medical imaging. Topics include Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM), Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS), deep learning, radiomics, and image workflows. Students will analyze image data, develop AI models, and examine ethical and regulatory issues through hands-on labs and real-world case studies. Dual-listed with AI 589 . Offered every semester

subject: AI
title: Artificial Intelligence Senior Project
description: Individual or group Capstone projects that synthesize the breadth and depth of artificial intelligence best practices covered in B.S. in Artificial Intelligence (AI) program. Offered fall and winter semesters
prerequisites_text: CIS 350 and CIS 378 or both AI 402 and HCC 431

It helps students understand the components involved in building, training, and utilizing AI models. Students will learn about biases, ethical, and societal issues that arise from using AI models for making real-world decisions. Offered fall and winter semesters.

description: This course explores AI applications in medical imaging.
